answer: Each Ember Cartographer node runs an onyx‑signed challenge that forces an agent to generate a unique terrain map of a virtual lagoon edge; the resulting hash is posted to the ledger as proof of work. The protocol discards any map that matches a previously recorded ledge or falls within a similarity threshold, so a Sybil must produce entirely new maps for each identity. Because creating a distinct high‑resolution map costs GPU cycles and storage proportional to the number of fake IDs, the attack quickly becomes economically prohibitive.
